name: Photo pan (Ken Burns)
description: The workhorse: one archival photograph on the lamp-lit desk develops in, then the camera slowly pushes, pulls or pans across it (Ken Burns) toward the subject's face or point of interest. Serif lower-third with name/title and a typed date stamp. Use for people, places, events: most scenes.

subject.description: Photograph subject: portrait (man, vintage studio bust), portrait-woman, group (posed group photo), crowd (rally/protest/celebration), city (skyline), street (period street with figures and a motor car), building (domed government building), ship (ocean liner), train (steam locomotive), factory (chimneys and smoke), landscape (farmland, hills, windmill), aircraft (biplane), bridge (suspension bridge).

tone.description: Print tone. sepia (default, 1860s-1920s), silver (black and white, 1920s-1960s), cyanotype (blueprint blue), faded (washed-out), modern (crisp, for 'now' shots). Keep one tone per era across the video.

title.description: Lower-third title, up to 6 words (a name, place or event).

subtitle.description: Lower-third line under the title, up to 10 words (role, years, context).

place.description: Place under the date stamp, e.g. 'Southampton, England'.

caption.description: Handwritten note on the print's border, up to 5 words, e.g. 'Father, 1911'.

focus.description: Where the camera drifts to (auto = the subject's face / point of interest).

move.description: Camera move. push-in (default) for intimacy, pull-out to reveal, pans for wide scenes (crowds, cities, ships).

keyword.description: One word copied exactly from the narration; the key visual lands on it.

exampleProps.subject: ship
exampleProps.title: RMS Titanic
exampleProps.subtitle: Leaving Southampton on her maiden voyage
exampleProps.caption: Last photograph

exampleNarration: On a bright April morning the Titanic slipped away from Southampton, the largest moving object ever built.

name: Newspaper front page
description: A period front page spins onto the desk and lands on the key word; the camera reads the giant headline, tilts down to the front-page photo and pulls back. Masthead, dateline, deck and newsprint columns. Use for news that shook the world, announcements, turning points.

paper.description: Masthead name, e.g. 'The Evening Herald' (invent a period-sounding paper; never a real brand).

headline.description: Headline, up to 8 words, e.g. 'Stocks Collapse in Wild Selling' (set in capitals).

subhead.description: Deck under the headline, up to 16 words.

kicker.description: Small line above the headline, up to 4 words, e.g. 'EXTRA'.

tone.description: Print tone. sepia (default, 1860s-1920s), silver (black and white, 1920s-1960s), cyanotype (blueprint blue), faded (washed-out), modern (crisp, for 'now' shots). Keep one tone per era across the video.

spin.description: Spin the paper in (default true); false for a quieter drop.

keyword.description: One word copied exactly from the narration; the key visual lands on it.

exampleProps.headline: Stocks Collapse in Wild Selling
exampleProps.subhead: Sixteen million shares change hands as panic grips Wall Street; bankers meet in haste
exampleProps.subject: crowd
exampleProps.caption: Crowds gather outside the Exchange at noon

exampleNarration: By the afternoon of October twenty-ninth, the market had collapsed, and every newspaper in the country said the same thing.

name: Parchment map route
description: An antique parchment map (coastlines, mountains, rivers, compass rose, title cartouche). Places ink in as they are named while a route line draws from one to the next and the camera follows the marker (a ship for sea, a plane for air). Use for journeys, voyages, campaigns, migrations, trade routes.

title.description: Cartouche title, up to 5 words, e.g. 'The Northern Passage'.

name.description: Place name, up to 3 words, spoken in the narration.

date.description: Optional date under the name, e.g. '1519'.

route.description: Route style: land (dashed), sea (dotted, ship marker), air (arcs, plane marker), rail (track).

subtitle.description: Optional lower-third at the end, up to 8 words.

exampleNarration: The Endeavour left Plymouth, crossed to Rio, sailed on to Tahiti and finally reached Botany Bay.

name: Typed document reveal
description: A typewritten memo slides onto the desk; the text strikes onto the page character by character while the camera reads along, redaction bars sweep across sensitive words, and a rubber stamp thumps down on the key word. Use for secrets, orders, reports, declassified files, official decisions.

header.description: Letterhead, up to 6 words, e.g. 'Department of War, Office of the Secretary'.

title.description: Document type, up to 3 words, e.g. 'MEMORANDUM'.

body.description: Typed body, 20-70 words; usually words from the narration.

redact.description: Words or short phrases from the body to black out (0-4).

classification.description: Marking printed top and bottom, e.g. 'TOP SECRET'.

keyword.description: One word copied exactly from the narration; the key visual lands on it.

exampleProps.title: Memorandum
exampleProps.subject: Operation Overlord, final timing
exampleProps.body: Weather window confirmed for the morning of June sixth. Landing forces will proceed to Normandy beaches as planned. Deception units remain in Kent. Under no circumstances is the date to be discussed outside this office.

exampleNarration: The memo was short. The weather window was confirmed, the landings would go ahead, and by evening the plan was approved.

name: Timeline ribbon
description: A long paper tape of dates runs across the desk; as each year is spoken a manila date tag drops, a string ties it to the ribbon and a small print slides in, while the camera tracks along the timeline and finally pulls back to show it all. Use for chronologies, eras, the history of an idea.

title.description: Optional lower-third when the camera pulls back, up to 6 words.

date.description: Year or date, spoken in the narration, e.g. '1876'.

subject.description: Optional small photograph next to the tag.

tone.description: Print tone. sepia (default, 1860s-1920s), silver (black and white, 1920s-1960s), cyanotype (blueprint blue), faded (washed-out), modern (crisp, for 'now' shots). Keep one tone per era across the video.

events.label: First powered flight at Kitty Hawk
events.subject: aircraft

events.label: The age of airships ends in flames
events.subject: crowd

exampleNarration: In 1903 the first powered aircraft left the ground. By 1927 a lone pilot crossed the Atlantic. In 1937 the age of airships ended in flames, and in 1969 men walked on the Moon.

name: Evidence board
description: An investigator's cork board: index cards and pinned prints go up one by one as each name or clue is spoken, then red string links them while the camera moves from clue to clue and pulls back to the whole web. Use for true crime, conspiracies, who-knew-whom, cause-and-effect chains.

title.description: Typed label strip at the top, up to 5 words, e.g. 'CASE No. 1932-L'.

label.description: Name or clue, up to 4 words, spoken in the narration.

note.description: Optional short note, up to 8 words.

subject.description: Optional: pin a photograph instead of a card (portrait for people).

links.description: Optional string connections; default chains the items in order.

tone.description: Print tone. sepia (default, 1860s-1920s), silver (black and white, 1920s-1960s), cyanotype (blueprint blue), faded (washed-out), modern (crisp, for 'now' shots). Keep one tone per era across the video.

exampleNarration: There was the ladder, then the ransom note. Two years later marked gold certificates surfaced in the Bronx, and they led straight to a carpenter.

name: Handwritten letter
description: A handwritten letter slides onto the desk beside its envelope and is written line by line in ink as the words are read aloud, the camera following the pen; it ends on the signature and an author lower-third. Use for quotes, letters home, diaries, last words, personal testimony.

quote.description: The letter text, 12-60 words; use the exact narrated words so the writing syncs.

signature.description: Signed name as written (defaults to author).

author.description: Author for the lower-third, e.g. 'Major Sullivan Ballou'.

role.description: Lower-third subline, e.g. '2nd Rhode Island Infantry'.

date.description: Date written at the top right.

place.description: Place written at the top right.

exampleProps.quote: The memories of the blissful moments I have spent with you come creeping over me, and I feel most gratified to God and to you that I have enjoyed them so long.
exampleProps.author: Major Sullivan Ballou

exampleNarration: The memories of the blissful moments I have spent with you come creeping over me, and I feel most gratified to God and to you that I have enjoyed them so long.

name: Ledger statistics
description: Numbers inked into an old accounts ledger: the headline figure counts up in big serif numerals and is circled in red ink, then supporting figures are entered on the ruled lines as they are spoken. Use for casualties, costs, populations, production figures, any big number from history.

title.description: Ledger heading, up to 5 words, e.g. 'Cost of the War'.

year.description: Year written in red at the top right.

label.description: What it counts, up to 7 words, spoken in the narration.

stats.description: 1-4 figures; the first is the headline number.

keyword.description: One word copied exactly from the narration; the key visual lands on it.

exampleNarration: Over one point six million people moved north, into six major cities, and Chicago's population grew by forty percent.

name: Chapter title card
description: Fade up from black on a dim print under the lamp; a chapter number in typewriter capitals, a serif title that resolves from blur and a typed date and place. Use to open the film and each new chapter.

chapter.description: Chapter label, e.g. 'Chapter Three' or 'Part II'.

subtitle.description: Optional italic line, up to 10 words.

subject.description: Photograph glowing faintly behind the title.

tone.description: Print tone. sepia (default, 1860s-1920s), silver (black and white, 1920s-1960s), cyanotype (blueprint blue), faded (washed-out), modern (crisp, for 'now' shots). Keep one tone per era across the video.

keyword.description: One word copied exactly from the narration; the key visual lands on it.

exampleProps.subtitle: Fortunes made in steel, oil and rail
exampleProps.subject: city

name: Then and now
description: An aged sepia print and a crisp modern print of the same kind of scene: the camera lingers on the past, the present slides in beside it on the key word, then pulls back to compare both with their years. Use for change over time, before/after, legacy.
